* * *

## Sum of interior angles of a polygon

You know that the sum of interior angles of a triangle is equal to  180°  (see the lesson  [Sum of the interior angles of a triangle]   in this site).

You,  probably,  also know that the sum of interior angles of a parallelogram,  a trapezoid and even any arbitrary quadrilateral is equal to  360°.

In this lesson you will learn that the sum of interior angles of any convex n-sided convex polygon equals  (n-2)\*180°.

For example,  the sum of interior angles of any convex pentagon is  540°.

The sum of interior angles of any convex hexagon is  720°.

### Theorem

The sum of interior angles of an n-sided convex polygon equals  (n-2)\*180°.

| | | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Proof** Let  **A1A2A3...An**  be a convex polygon in a plane with  **n**  vertices  **A1**,  **A2**,                        **A3**, . . . ,  **An**  and  **n**  sides. It is shown in the  **Figure 1a**  for  **n** =6  as an example. Let us draw the diagonals  **A1A3**,  **A1A4**, . . . ,  **A1A(n-1)**  in the given polygon **A1A2A3...An**  connecting the vertex  **A1**  with the consecutive vertices **A3**,  **A4**, . . . ,  **A(n-1)**.  In total,  there are  n-2  such diagonals.  They all lie inside the polygon,  because the polygon is convex. These diagonals divide the polygon in  n-2  triangles  **A1A2A3**,  **A1A3A4**, . . . , **A1A(n-1)An**. | ![] **Figure 1a**. To the **Theorem 1** | ![] **Figure 1b**. To the proof of the **Theorem 1** |

Each of these triangles has the sum of interior angles of  180°,  and the sum of interior angles of the polygon is equal to the sum of all interior angles of these  n-2

triangles,  i.e.  (n-2)\*180°.

The  **Theorem**  is proved.

### Corollary

The interior angle of a regular n-sides polygon is of   ![%28n-2%29%2Fn].180°.

**Proof**

Indeed,  the sum of all interior angles of a  n-sided polygon is  (n-2)\*180°  in accordance with the  **Theorem 1**  above.  In the regular polygon all internal angles are congruent.

Therefore,  the measure of each individual interior angle in the regular  n-sided polygon is of   ![%28n-2%29%2Fn].180°.

Thus,  for example,  the interior angle of a regular triangle  (n=3)  is of   ![1%2F3].180° = 60°.

The interior angle of a regular quadrilateral  (square,  n=4)  is of   ![2%2F4].180° = 90°.

The interior angle of a regular pentagon  (n=5)  is of   ![3%2F5].180° = 108°.

A regular hexagon  (n=6)  has the interior angle of   ![4%2F6].180° = 120°.

A regular octagon  (n=8)  has the interior angle of   ![6%2F8].180° = 135°.

### Example 1

Find the sum of interior angles of an  10-sided convex polygon.

**Solution**

According to the  **Theorem 1**  the sum of interior angles of an  10-sided polygon is  (10-2)\*180° = 8\*180° = 1440°.

**Answer**.  The sum of interior angles of  10-sided polygon is of  1440°.

### Example 2

Find the fifth interior angle of a convex pentagon if it has four interior angles of  65°,  95°,  110° and  130°.

**Solution**

According to the  **Theorem 1**  the sum of five interior angles of a  5-sided convex polygon is of  (5-2)\*180° = 3\*180° = 540°.

Therefore,  to find the unknown fifth angle we need to distract the sum of the four given angles from 540°:  the unknown angle is

540° - (65° + 95° + 110° + 130°) = 540° - 400° = 140°.

**Answer**.  The fifth missed angle of the pentagon is of  140°.
